audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Filtered projection has negative U exponents on an allowed domain element; Naive totalization of a general hyperbox need not square to zero; Unqualified finite-dimensional F_2 quasi-isomorphic replacement cannot preserve completed minus homology
limitations: F01 — Filtered projection has negative U exponents on an allowed domain element — Counterevidence: Neither nonnegative power-series completion nor sparse-grid restrictions admit the image. Infinity Laurent coefficients are a different theory. No reindexing is stated for the same generator and parameter.

F01 — Filtered projection has negative U exponents on an allowed domain element — Limit: This invalidates a printed core construction as stated, not the underlying computability conclusion. Journal status is unverified.

F01 — Filtered projection has negative U exponents on an allowed domain element — Counterevidence: Completion only permits infinite sums of nonnegative powers. The infinity ring is separately defined. The knot orientation equal to the removed whole sublink gives the same exponent in the projection-inclusion map.

F02 — Naive totalization of a general hyperbox need not square to zero — Counterevidence: For unit hypercubes every possible endpoint displacement is covered by equation (1). Compression produces the two-term identity map in this example and repairs the differential.
F02 — Naive totalization of a general hyperbox need not square to zero — Limit: Peripheral overgeneralization; not evidence against the later compressed surgery formula.

F02 — Naive totalization of a general hyperbox need not square to zero — Counterevidence: Unit cubes satisfy all endpoint relations and later descent explicitly uses compression. The surgery indexing is by sublinks and is a unit cube.

F03 — Unqualified finite-dimensional F_2 quasi-isomorphic replacement cannot preserve completed minus homology — Counterevidence: Finite rank/presentation over F_2[[U]], finite grading windows, and degreewise algorithms are possible; they are distinct from the unqualified global finite-dimensional assertion. Discussion of ranks elsewhere suggests an intended restriction but does not supply it.

F03 — Unqualified finite-dimensional F_2 quasi-isomorphic replacement cannot preserve completed minus homology — Limit: Computability itself is not refuted. A finite encoding or degreewise repair has not been independently verified. The external truncation proof and the journal version have not been fully checked.

F03 — Unqualified finite-dimensional F_2 quasi-isomorphic replacement cannot preserve completed minus homology — Counterevidence: Finite rank or finite presentation over F2[[U]], fixed-degree truncation and finite algorithmic encoding remain compatible. They are not the stated global finite F2 dimension; surrounding rank language does not insert a restriction into the exact claim.

proposition.claim:
The R-linear projection from the printed filtered part F_i <= s_i is a resolution of the ordinary Alexander-filtered minus complex.

One O per row/column, at most one X, free-O condition, q=2, separated X rows and columns including cyclic adjacency, one linked component, integer Alexander lattice, finite monomial satisfies completion boundedness.

The sum of all local hyperbox maps is a differential on the uncompressed total space.

All required map degrees hold. Relations at displacements zero and one are zero; no displacement-two relation is imposed.

The completed minus surgery complex can be replaced by a quasi-isomorphic finite-dimensional complex over F_2.
